recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. Revisit only if CQI/TSMG later finalizes production THO terminology for measure-stratifier-type and opens a final Core issue to replace or rebind the example terminology.
issue_request: FHIR-51028 was an Applied CQI change request for R6. The initial proposal asked to remove example labeling and experimental flags from the measure-stratifier CodeSystem and ValueSet, but the final Persuasive with Modification resolution kept a clearly labeled Core example and requested renaming measure-stratifier-example to measure-stratifier-type-example, changing age to age-range, changing region to facility, and updating affected names, ids, URLs, and references.
initial_application: HL7/fhir PR #4050 applied the issue. Commit 18df653fdc321d3e20a95d14638e59a6d41168d7 renamed the CodeSystem and ValueSet source files and canonical URLs, updated Measure and MeasureReport bindings, updated OID entries, and changed the concepts to age-range, gender, and facility. Commit f43fbf565a77bf872216d73bce2ef961e739462c then added Measure and MeasureReport ballot notes describing FHIR-51028 as clarifying that examples are experimental content.
additional_context: Measure and MeasureReport are active resources in source/fhir.ini, so their terminology sources and bindings are in current build scope. The TSMG minutes cited by the Jira issue establish the policy concern for example code systems in THO while noting that experimental is the appropriate signal for example code system intent in IG contexts. Jira comments and the follow-up ballot note support retaining a clearly labeled experimental example in Core while production Measure Stratifier Type terminology matures in QM/THO work outside this core checkout.
reconciliation: No source changes were made. Current source already uses measure-stratifier-type-example for the CodeSystem, ValueSet, OIDs, Measure bindings, MeasureReport bindings, and Measure $evaluate parameter binding. The concepts include age-range and facility as requested. The retained experimental=true values are consistent with the final modified resolution and the applied follow-up note, so changing them here would go beyond the final work-group decision.
